data.narrative:
The Lumber Manufactory is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $53.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 9 comparable companies: 1 public (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Hadrian, Agile Robots, and Nimble Robotics, all at Series C stage within the same sector.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression modeling uses total capital raised ($53M) as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $90M. Peer-median analysis across three same-stage, same-sector comparables—Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B)—produces a median of $1.0B with a range of $1.0B to $1.6B.

The two methods diverge significantly, reflecting fundamental differences in approach: stage-progression anchors to actual capital deployed, while peer-median reflects market pricing for comparable-stage robotics firms. The triangulated range spans $77M (conservative stage-progression floor) to $1.1B (peer-based ceiling), with a median of $545M. The wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty around whether The Lumber Manufactory's technology, market traction, or capital efficiency justifies peer-median valuations. Resolution requires clarity on revenue scale, customer concentration, and unit economics relative to Hadrian and peers.
